prompt.context_jp: 美紀が久しぶりに会社へ出勤した最初の日、山村家のリビングには和之と理絵だけ___残されていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 山村家のリビングには和之と理絵だけ___残されていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits after 「だけ」 (only Kazuyuki and Rie were left).

feedback.correct_en: 「だけが残されていた」 presents new information identifying exactly who was left — an exhaustive-listing use of が. The focus is on identifying the remaining people.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 「和之と理絵だけ」 a topic already known, which doesn't fit this scene-opening descriptive sentence. を would be ungrammatical with the passive 残されていた.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋には私だけが残った。
contrast_examples.en: Only I was left in the room. (identifying who)
As for me, I already went home. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 和之___、ついこの間までCMディレクターとして撮影現場を仕切っていた男である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 和之___、ついこの間までCMディレクターとして撮影現場を仕切っていた男である。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for introducing Kazuyuki as the topic of a descriptive statement.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is giving background info about Kazuyuki as the established topic ('As for Kazuyuki, he is a man who...'). This は sets up the topic for the predicate that follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark him as newly identified info, but here he's already the known protagonist. に doesn't fit the copula structure.

contrast_examples.en: He is a kind person. (topic description)

contrast_examples.jp: 優しいのは彼が一番だ。
contrast_examples.en: When it comes to kindness, he is the top. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: ところが仕事の依頼___大幅に減少し、気がつけば妻と立場を入れ替えることになっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ところが仕事の依頼___大幅に減少し…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces new information.

feedback.correct_en: 「ところが」 signals a new turn; 「仕事の依頼」 is newly introduced information with が marking the subject of the event 減少し.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 'job requests' as an already-established topic, which clashes with ところが introducing a surprising new development. を is wrong because 減少する is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: The rain has already stopped. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: だが実際に___、洗濯ひとつ始めるにも何から手をつければいいのか見当がつかない。
prompt.prompt_jp: だが実際に___、洗濯ひとつ始めるにも…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the contrast 「だが実際___」.

feedback.correct_en: 「実際には」 sets up a contrastive topic ('but in reality, by contrast with what he thought'). は after に makes the contrast with his earlier attitude explicit.
feedback.incorrect_en: が cannot attach this way to に to express contrast. で alone would lose the contrastive nuance signaled by だが.

contrast_examples.jp: 口では強いが、実際には弱い。
contrast_examples.en: Tough in words, but weak in reality. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 部屋の中に、気まずい沈黙___落ちた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋の中に、気まずい沈黙___落ちた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the subject of this scene-setting event.

feedback.correct_en: The silence is new, unexpected information arising in the scene — classic 'event が'. It presents the silence as a fresh occurrence the reader is just now witnessing.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the silence a known topic, but it's being introduced here for the first time. を doesn't work with intransitive 落ちる.

contrast_examples.jp: その沈黙はとても長かった。
contrast_examples.en: That silence was very long. (already-known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 悔しさを隠しきれず、膝の上で握った拳___わずかに震えている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 膝の上で握った拳___わずかに震えている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the subject of the trembling.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator zooms in on a newly observed detail — 'his clenched fist is trembling' — descriptive new info, so が. It's a cinematic 'look at this' moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply 'as for the fist (vs. other things)', treating it as an established topic, which doesn't match the vivid descriptive mode.

contrast_examples.en: His voice has now calmed down. (topic contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 仕事の世界では、自分の指示にスタッフ___黙って従うのが当たり前になっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の指示にスタッフ___黙って従うのが当たり前になっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the subject inside this embedded clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate clause before の (nominalizer), が is the standard subject marker. The sentence describes a fact/state ('staff following silently') without topicalization.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside an embedded nominalized clause would break the structure — は tends to take the matrix scope, not embedded. を is wrong since 従う takes に.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来るのを待っていた。
contrast_examples.en: I was waiting for him to come. (embedded subject)

prompt.context_jp: 窓の外では、隣家の洗濯物___のんきに風に揺れていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 窓の外では、隣家の洗濯物___のんきに風に揺れていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this descriptive scene.

feedback.correct_en: A descriptive scene-painting sentence: the laundry is newly observed detail, so が. The 窓の外では frame sets location, then が introduces what's visible there.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would single out 'the laundry' as a known topic in contrast, which doesn't match this fresh descriptive moment.

contrast_examples.en: Flowers were blooming in the garden. (newly observed)
Those flowers have already withered. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 理絵___不安そうに、父親と杉尾の顔を交互に見上げている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 理絵___不安そうに、父親と杉尾の顔を交互に見上げている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. Rie is newly brought into the scene.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator pans to Rie as a newly salient figure in the tense scene. が introduces her action as a fresh observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat Rie as the established topic being described in contrast to the men's exchange, which is a possible read but breaks the scenic 'now look at Rie' flow the narrator uses.

prompt.context_jp: 和之___内心、プライドを曲げた自分に舌打ちしたい気分だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 和之___内心、プライドを曲げた自分に舌打ちしたい気分だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Kazuyuki as the ongoing topic.

feedback.correct_en: Kazuyuki is the established protagonist whose inner feelings the narrator continues to describe. は signals topic-continuation about him.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark him as newly identified, but he's been the focus for many sentences. を doesn't fit the subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 悔しがったのは彼だった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who was frustrated was him. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: 「ああ すいません この洗濯機 ちょっと調子悪いらしくて― 水___出ないんですよね 今」
prompt.prompt_jp: 水___出ないんですよね
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. Kazuyuki is reporting a problem.

feedback.correct_en: Reporting a newly noticed problem — 'water isn't coming out!' The water is new, descriptive info, so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「水は出ない」 would sound like a general characterization contrasting water with something else. In an urgent complaint about a broken state, が is natural.

contrast_examples.en: Hot water isn't coming out! (reporting a problem)

contrast_examples.jp: お湯は出るけど水は出ない。
contrast_examples.en: Hot water comes out, but cold water doesn't. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 家事は一つ終わると次___待っていて、少しでも手を止めればたちまち仕事が滞っていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 家事は一つ終わると次___待っていて…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 「次」 (the next chore).

feedback.correct_en: 「家事は」 is the topic; within the comment, 「次が待っていて」 introduces 'the next one' as new info — a classic は...が pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would create two topics in the same clause, which is awkward. The subject of 待っている here needs が.

contrast_examples.en: This town has many people. (topic は, subject が)

prompt.context_jp: 一方の杉尾___、鼻歌まじりで床を磨き上げ、棚のほこりまで丁寧に拭き取っていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一方の杉尾___、鼻歌まじりで床を磨き上げ…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. Sugio is being contrasted with Kazuyuki.

feedback.correct_en: 「一方の」 explicitly sets up a contrast. は is the contrastive-topic marker: 'Kazuyuki was struggling; Sugio, on the other hand, was humming.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark Sugio as newly identified rather than contrasted with the already-established Kazuyuki. In a 一方 construction, は is standard.

contrast_examples.jp: 兄は静かだが、弟は騒がしい。
contrast_examples.en: The older brother is quiet; the younger, loud. (contrast は)

contrast_examples.jp: 騒いでいるのは弟が一人だ。
contrast_examples.en: The one making noise is the younger brother. (identification が)

prompt.context_jp: 「どっち___簡単なんですけど」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「どっち___簡単なんですけど」
prompt.prompt_en: Sugio is replying that both shrimp fry and hamburgers are easy.

feedback.correct_en: 「どっちも」 = 'both'. Sugio deflates Kazuyuki's assumption by saying 'both of them are actually easy'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「どっちが」 would ask 'which one'. 「どっちは」 is ungrammatical here.

prompt.context_jp: 一円でも安いもの___選ぼうとするその姿は、まるで熟練の主婦そのものだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一円でも安いもの___選ぼうとするその姿は…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the object of 選ぶ.

feedback.correct_en: 選ぶ (to choose) takes a direct object, marked with を. 'Trying to choose the cheapest item by even one yen'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the subject, but 'thing' is what's being chosen. に doesn't fit the transitive verb.

prompt.context_jp: 次の瞬間、彼女の足___ぴたりと止まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 次の瞬間、彼女の足___ぴたりと止まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this dramatic moment.

feedback.correct_en: A sudden, cinematic event — 'her feet stopped' — presented as new, observed information. が highlights the surprise of the moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'her feet' a topic, flattening the dramatic abruptness the narrator is building with 次の瞬間.

prompt.context_jp: 「今は ただの___主夫でしょう」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「今は ただの___主夫でしょう」
prompt.prompt_en: Sugio is telling Kazuyuki he's just a beginner at housework.

feedback.correct_en: 新米 (しんまい) literally 'new rice' is the set expression for 'rookie / newbie' in a profession. 新米主夫 = 'rookie househusband'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 新品 means 'brand-new item' (for objects, not people). 新顔 means 'new face' but doesn't collocate naturally with 主夫.

prompt.context_jp: 家事など誰にでもできる、と彼はずっと___をくくってきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 家事など誰にでもできる、と彼はずっと___をくくってきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for 'underestimate'.

feedback.correct_en: 高をくくる is the set idiom meaning 'to underestimate / make light of'. Kazuyuki has long underestimated housework.
feedback.incorrect_en: 腹をくくる means 'to resolve oneself / brace oneself' — opposite nuance. 気をくくる is not a set phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: 簡単だと高をくくっていた。
contrast_examples.en: I underestimated it, thinking it would be easy.
I braced myself and took it on.

prompt.context_jp: ___も積もれば山となる、とはよく言ったものだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___も積もれば山となる
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the proverb (even small things add up).

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる ('even dust piles up into a mountain') is the fixed proverb. The chapter uses it as a thematic motif.
feedback.incorrect_en: 砂 (sand) and 雪 (snow) can pile up literally but aren't the set form of the proverb.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.

prompt.context_jp: 恥ずかしさをごまかしきれず、彼は___をひとつしてその場を取り繕った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼は___をひとつしてその場を取り繕った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose what Kazuyuki does to cover his embarrassment.

feedback.correct_en: 咳払い (clearing one's throat) is the standard gesture to mask embarrassment or buy time. It fits 取り繕う perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: あくび (yawn) suggests boredom, not embarrassment. 深呼吸 (deep breath) suggests calming down before action, not covering a slip.

contrast_examples.jp: 咳払いしてごまかした。
contrast_examples.en: He cleared his throat to cover it up.

contrast_examples.jp: 深呼吸して落ち着いた。
contrast_examples.en: He took a deep breath and calmed down.

prompt.context_jp: 和之は初めてかすかな___の念を抱いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 和之は初めてかすかな___の念を抱いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for the feeling of awe/respect toward housewives.

feedback.correct_en: 畏敬の念 (いけいのねん) = 'a sense of awe/reverence'. Having struggled through chores, Kazuyuki feels respect for housewives.
feedback.incorrect_en: 嫉妬 (jealousy) and 軽蔑 (contempt) don't fit — he's gaining respect, not scorning or envying them.

contrast_examples.jp: 自然に畏敬の念を抱く。

prompt.context_jp: 「“___”ってやつが 必要なんじゃないですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「“___”ってやつが 必要なんじゃないですか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Sugio tells Kazuyuki what quality he needs.

feedback.correct_en: 謙虚さ (humility) is what Sugio tells the arrogant Kazuyuki he needs. It's the chapter's thematic keyword (title: プライドを曲げて).
feedback.incorrect_en: 傲慢さ (arrogance) is the opposite — what Kazuyuki already has too much of. 厳しさ (strictness) doesn't fit the context of bending one's pride.

contrast_examples.jp: 傲慢な態度は嫌われる。

prompt.context_jp: 和之は___を隠しきれず、わざと手元に集中するふりをした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 和之は___を隠しきれず、わざと手元に集中するふりをした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the emotion Kazuyuki is trying to hide when his daughter watches him cook.

feedback.correct_en: 照れくささ (embarrassment / bashfulness) fits — Rie seeing her dad cook for the first time makes him flustered in an endearing way.
feedback.incorrect_en: 怒り (anger) doesn't match the warm tone. 眠気 (sleepiness) doesn't fit either.

prompt.context_jp: その一言が、和之の胸に___刺さった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その一言が、和之の胸に___刺さった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the onomatopoeia for a small sharp pang.

feedback.correct_en: ちくりと刺さる = 'pricks sharply (like a needle)' — standard for a small, pointed emotional hurt. Miki's 'thank you' pierces his guilty conscience.
feedback.incorrect_en: ぐっすり is for sleeping deeply. のんびり is 'leisurely'. Neither fits the sharp emotional sting.

contrast_examples.jp: 心にちくりと刺さる言葉。

prompt.context_jp: Kazuyuki finally swallows his pride and asks Sugio for help.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as Kazuyuki reluctantly asking for help?

choices.text: すいませんけど あの… 手伝ってください
すいませんけど あの… 手伝ってほしい
すいませんけど あの… 手伝え

feedback.correct_en: Kazuyuki needs to swallow his pride and make a clear polite request. 「手伝ってください」 is the natural polite request matching the show's actual line.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「手伝ってほしい」 is a statement of desire, awkward as a direct request. 「手伝え」 is a blunt command — the opposite of the humility Sugio demanded.

contrast_examples.jp: 手伝ってほしいんですが。
contrast_examples.en: I'd like you to help me, but... (softer, indirect)

prompt.context_jp: Sugio realizes Kazuyuki never turned on the faucet.
prompt.prompt_en: Which is the most natural way to express 'If you don't turn on the faucet, no water will come out'?

choices.text: 蛇口を開けないで 水が出るわけ… ないですよね
蛇口を開けなくて 水が出るわけ… ないですよね
蛇口を開けずに 水を出るわけ… ないですよね

feedback.correct_en: 「〜ないで + 〜わけがない」 is the idiomatic way to say 'there's no way X without doing Y'. This matches the drama's actual line.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「開けなくて」 would express a cause/reason, sounding awkward here. In option c, 「水を出る」 is wrong — 出る is intransitive and takes が, not を.

contrast_examples.jp: 傘を持たないで出かけた。
contrast_examples.en: I went out without an umbrella. (ないで = without)
I had no umbrella and was in trouble. (なくて = reason)

prompt.context_jp: Sugio casually mentions he has a dryer. Kazuyuki responds with frustration.
prompt.prompt_en: Which response sounds most natural for exasperated Kazuyuki?

choices.text: いや それ 早く言ってくださいよ
いや それ 早く言えばよかったでしょう
いや それ 早く言ってもいいでしょう

feedback.correct_en: 「〜てくださいよ」 with よ expresses the natural, slightly complaining tone of 'you should have told me earlier!' — matching Kazuyuki's frustrated reaction.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b sounds like an abstract past-conditional judgment, oddly detached. Option c means 'you're allowed to say it early', missing the complaint nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 早く言ってくださいよ。
早く言ってもらえますか。
contrast_examples.en: Could you tell me sooner? (polite request)

prompt.context_jp: Kazuyuki finally confesses to Miki that he had help.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for a reluctant, hesitant confession?

choices.text: 実は あの… 手伝ってもらったんだよ
実は あの… 手伝ってあげたんだよ
実は あの… 手伝ったんだよ

feedback.correct_en: 「手伝ってもらった」 (received help) correctly conveys that Sugio helped him. The 〜てもらう form captures the humble admission.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「手伝ってあげた」 means 'I helped (someone else)' — the opposite direction. 「手伝った」 also means he did the helping, contradicting the confession.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼に手伝ってもらった。

prompt.context_jp: Kazuyuki waves off Rie's offer to help, trying to sound capable.
prompt.prompt_en: Which is the most natural father-to-child casual speech?

choices.text: 理絵 大丈夫だ パパ一人で やるから
理絵さん 大丈夫です パパが一人で やりますから
理絵 大丈夫である パパ一人で やるので

feedback.correct_en: Plain-form, name-only address matches a father speaking warmly to his young daughter. This is the actual line.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b with 〜さん and です/ます is way too formal for a dad talking to his small child. Option c's である is written/formal register, unnatural in speech.

contrast_examples.jp: 大丈夫だ、パパがやるよ。
contrast_examples.en: It's okay, Daddy will do it. (casual, warm)

contrast_examples.jp: 大丈夫です、私がやります。
contrast_examples.en: It's fine, I will do it. (polite, distant)
